central_node: Green School Campus, Waste Segregation, and Environmental Audits

key_details: An eco-friendly school campus promoting sustainability
Practices waste management, resource saving, and nature care
Creates a safe, clean, and happy learning environment
real_world_examples: Swachh Bharat Swachh Vidyalaya campaign initiatives

key_details: Wet Waste: Biodegradable organic items like fruit peels and food scraps
Dry Waste: Non-biodegradable recyclables like paper, plastic, and glass
Disposed of in green (wet) and blue (dry) bins
Source segregation protects sanitation workers from sharp objects
Prevents dry recyclable paper from getting soiled by organic rot
Enables traditional recyclers (kabadiwalas) to process dry waste
real_world_examples: Composting organic kitchen waste in school gardens

key_details: Painting building roofs with light or white reflective paint
High albedo reflects shortwave solar radiation away
Lowers classroom indoor temperatures without heavy electricity use
real_world_examples: White reflective roof coatings on school buildings

key_details: Inspecting taps and pipes for slow drips
A tap leaking 1 drop per second wastes over 4 liters daily
real_world_examples: Student-led plumbing audit in school restrooms
